seo.title: Best Dessert Cafes in Casablanca (2026) | tabiji.ai
seo.metaDescription: Discover Casablanca's top dessert cafes and patisseries. From traditional Moroccan sweets to French pastries and artisanal gelato, find your perfect sweet escape.

hero.subtitle: Casablanca, a bustling metropolis, offers a surprising array of sweet havens, from historic patisseries to modern cafes, perfect for satisfying any dessert craving.

picks.name: Amoud
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Amoud is a Casablanca institution, celebrated for its exquisite range of French and Moroccan pastries. Their commitment to quality ingredients and artisanal techniques results in consistently delicious creations, from delicate macarons to rich operasa. The spacious cafes are perfect for a leisurely afternoon coffee and treat.
picks.whatToOrder: Opera Cake or Cornes de Gazelle
picks.insiderTip: Amoud's larger branches often have a separate counter for fresh bread and savories, perfect for picking up items for a picnic or light lunch.
picks.redditQuote: "You can't go wrong with Amoud, their mille-feuille is next level and their Moroccan pastries are always fresh. It's my go-to for special occasions."

picks.name: Pâtisserie Bennis Habous
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Located in the historic Habous district, Bennis Habous is a legendary patisserie famous for its authentic Moroccan sweets. This no-frills shop focuses entirely on quality, offering a dizzying array of traditional cookies and pastries made with almonds, honey, and orange blossom water. It's a true taste of Moroccan heritage.
picks.insiderTip: Go early in the day for the freshest selection, as items often sell out quickly. It's a takeaway spot, so plan to enjoy your treats elsewhere.
picks.redditQuote: "Pâtisserie Bennis Habous is the real deal for Moroccan sweets. Forget the fancy places, this is where the locals go. Get a mixed box!"

picks.name: Paul
picks.whyItMadeTheList: The French bakery chain Paul brings a touch of Parisian elegance to Casablanca. Known for its rustic breads, flaky croissants, and classic French pastries, Paul offers a reliable and delicious experience. It's an ideal spot for a leisurely breakfast or a coffee break with a view, providing a consistent standard of quality.
picks.insiderTip: Their branch at AnfaPlace Mall offers ocean views, making it a pleasant spot to unwind after shopping. Grab a baguette to take home.
picks.redditQuote: "Paul in Casablanca is just as good as anywhere else. Always get their almond croissants, they're perfect with a strong coffee."

picks.name: Maison Saouma
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Maison Saouma offers a sophisticated take on both French and Moroccan pastries, presented with artistic flair. This high-end patisserie is known for its elegant creations and refined flavors, making it a destination for those seeking premium dessert experiences. The ambiance is chic, perfect for a refined indulgence.
picks.whatToOrder: Any of their individually crafted entremets or a selection of miniature Moroccan pastries.
picks.insiderTip: This spot is great for impressing clients or for a special treat. Their packaging is also beautiful if you're buying gifts.
picks.redditQuote: "Maison Saouma is a bit pricey but totally worth it for the quality. Their passion fruit tart was divine, really fresh and balanced."

picks.name: Oliveri
picks.whyItMadeTheList: For those craving authentic Italian gelato, Oliveri is the place to be. This popular spot serves up a wide variety of rich, creamy gelato flavors made with fresh ingredients. It's a local favorite, especially during warmer months, offering a refreshing and satisfying dessert experience in a lively neighborhood.
picks.insiderTip: They often have seasonal fruit flavors, so don't be afraid to ask for samples before committing to your scoop.
picks.redditQuote: "Oliveri has the best gelato in Casablanca, hands down. Their dark chocolate is so intense and the fruit flavors taste like actual fruit."

picks.name: La Croisée des Chemins
picks.whyItMadeTheList: La Croisée des Chemins is a cozy and welcoming cafe known for its relaxed atmosphere and good selection of pastries and cakes. It's a popular spot for locals to meet up for coffee, enjoy a casual dessert, and perhaps a light meal. The desserts are classic and comforting, perfect for a mid-day break.
picks.whatToOrder: Cheesecake or a classic Tarte Tatin
picks.insiderTip: They have outdoor seating, which is lovely on a sunny day. It can get busy during peak lunch hours, so plan accordingly for a dessert-focused visit.
picks.redditQuote: "Always enjoy a quiet afternoon at La Croisée des Chemins. Their fruit tarts are fresh and the coffee is strong, exactly what I need."

picks.name: Secret Garden by Zayna
picks.whyItMadeTheList: As its name suggests, Secret Garden by Zayna offers a beautiful, tranquil escape with stunning decor and a menu of contemporary desserts. This cafe is known for its aesthetically pleasing dishes and sophisticated ambiance, making it a prime spot for a special occasion or a delightful treat. Their creations are as beautiful as they are delicious.
picks.whatToOrder: Any of their signature plated desserts or the Red Velvet Cake
picks.insiderTip: Reservations are recommended, especially on weekends, as it's a very popular spot for brunch and afternoon tea. The garden area is truly charming.
picks.redditQuote: "Secret Garden by Zayna is gorgeous, seriously Instagram-worthy. The desserts are fancy and taste amazing. Great place for a girl's day out."

picks.name: Pâtisserie Madame Fati
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Pâtisserie Madame Fati is revered for its artisanal Moroccan pastries, particularly its exquisite baklava and other honey-nut based sweets. The emphasis here is on traditional recipes executed with precision and high-quality ingredients, resulting in rich, flavorful, and perfectly textured desserts that locals adore. It's a family-run business with a strong reputation.
picks.whatToOrder: Assorted Baklava or Kaab El Ghazal
picks.insiderTip: They also offer custom orders for events, so if you're hosting, keep them in mind. Their packaging is simple but elegant.
picks.redditQuote: "Madame Fati's baklava is legendary. Not too sweet, perfectly crisp and nutty. It's my go-to when I want authentic Moroccan treats."

picks.name: Brioche Dorée
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Brioche Dorée is a reliable and popular French chain offering a wide selection of viennoiseries, sandwiches, and pastries. It's a convenient spot for a quick coffee and a sweet treat, especially for those on the go or looking for a familiar taste. The Twin Center location is busy and offers good people-watching opportunities.
picks.whatToOrder: Pain au chocolat or a fruit tart
picks.insiderTip: Their lunch menu also offers good value if you want to pair your dessert with a savory option. Good for a quick stop rather than a lingering experience.
picks.redditQuote: "Brioche Dorée is my default for a fast breakfast pastry. Their coffee is decent and the pain au chocolat always hits the spot."

picks.name: Pâtisserie Le Vert Galant
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Le Vert Galant is a classic French patisserie offering a wide range of beautifully crafted cakes, individual pastries, and chocolates. It has a reputation for traditional recipes and elegant presentation, making it a favorite for celebrations or an upscale treat. The interior is sophisticated, reflecting its commitment to quality.
picks.whatToOrder: Black Forest Cake or an Eclair
picks.insiderTip: They make excellent custom cakes for birthdays and events. It's a bit more formal, so it's a good choice if you're looking for a quieter, more refined experience.
picks.redditQuote: "I always order my birthday cake from Le Vert Galant. Their cakes are consistently delicious and they look stunning. Worth the price."

picks.name: Delice Pâtisserie
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Delice Pâtisserie is a local gem, known for its affordable yet delicious range of traditional Moroccan and some French-inspired pastries. It's a humble shop focused on providing good quality at great prices, making it a favorite among residents in the Hay Hassani area. Expect a bustling atmosphere and fresh, comforting sweets.
picks.whatToOrder: Any of their Moroccan cookies sold by weight
picks.insiderTip: This is a great place to stock up on sweets if you're hosting. Bring cash, as smaller local places sometimes prefer it.
picks.redditQuote: "Delice Pâtisserie might not be fancy, but their stuff is always fresh and super cheap. Their almond cookies are addictive!"

picks.name: La Table du Marché
picks.whyItMadeTheList: While primarily a restaurant, La Table du Marché is renowned for its exceptional dessert menu, crafted by skilled pastry chefs. Their desserts are sophisticated and inventive, often incorporating fresh, seasonal ingredients with a French culinary backbone. It's an ideal choice for a luxurious post-dinner treat or a dedicated dessert experience in an upscale setting.
picks.whatToOrder: Their signature chocolate lava cake or a seasonal fruit tart
picks.insiderTip: This is a restaurant, so consider booking a table specifically for dessert and drinks in the evening. Dress code is smart casual.
picks.redditQuote: "If you want a truly gourmet dessert, La Table du Marché is incredible. Their take on a simple tarte tatin blew my mind. So refined."

faq.question: What are the most popular traditional Moroccan desserts in Casablanca?
faq.answer: Casablanca offers a delightful array of traditional Moroccan sweets. Must-tries include Kaab El Ghazal (gazelle horns), which are crescent-shaped pastries filled with almond paste, and Fekkas, dry cookies often studded with almonds or raisins. Chebakia, a honey-drenched, sesame-coated fried pastry, is especially popular during Ramadan but can often be found year-round at specialized patisseries like Pâtisserie Bennis Habous.

faq.question: Are there any gluten-free or vegan dessert options available?
faq.answer: While not all cafes specifically label their items as gluten-free or vegan, some establishments are beginning to cater to these dietary needs. Upscale cafes like Secret Garden by Zayna may offer more modern and inclusive options. It's always best to ask the staff directly about ingredients, especially for traditional Moroccan sweets which often contain nuts, honey, and sometimes dairy.

faq.question: What's the typical price range for desserts in Casablanca?
faq.answer: The price range for desserts in Casablanca varies widely. For traditional Moroccan sweets from local bakeries, you can expect to pay between 20-70 MAD ($2-7) for a few pieces or a small box. French-style pastries and desserts at mid-range cafes typically cost 50-120 MAD ($5-12), while high-end or gourmet desserts at luxury patisseries or restaurants can range from 100-200 MAD ($10-20) per item.

faq.question: Is tipping customary at dessert cafes in Casablanca?
faq.answer: Tipping is customary in Casablanca and is always appreciated, especially for good service. For a simple coffee and pastry at a casual cafe, leaving a few dirhams (5-10 MAD) is appropriate. At more upscale establishments or if you've had table service for a more elaborate dessert, a tip of 10% of the bill is a good guideline.

faq.question: What is the best time of day to visit dessert cafes in Casablanca?
faq.answer: The best time to visit dessert cafes depends on your preference. For a lively atmosphere and the freshest selection, late morning to early afternoon (10:00 AM - 3:00 PM) is ideal. Many locals enjoy afternoon tea or coffee with a pastry around 4:00 PM - 6:00 PM. If you prefer a quieter experience, try visiting right after opening or during the mid-afternoon lull before the evening rush.

faq.question: Do I need reservations for dessert cafes in Casablanca?
faq.answer: For most casual dessert cafes and patisseries, reservations are generally not necessary. You can simply walk in and find a seat. However, for popular spots known for their ambiance or for places that are primarily restaurants but offer excellent desserts, like Secret Garden by Zayna or La Table du Marché, making a reservation, especially on weekends or for evening visits, is highly recommended to secure a table.

methodology: Our selection of Casablanca's best dessert cafes was curated through extensive local research, online reviews, and expert recommendations. We prioritized venues known for their quality ingredients, unique offerings, inviting ambiance, and consistent customer satisfaction to ensure a delightful sweet journey.
